items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Leroy said in an article, “Can’t work in L.A. unless you’re a man, a friend” – or whatever it was, because it was Shelly Manne and His Men, Shorty Rogers and His Giants

ctx.x: André Previn and Shelly Manne. I remember Leroy telling me much later that – obviously, and it was justified, because sidemen don’t get royalties. The royalties go to the leader or to the people who write the music. I can remember starting to get a little bitter then. Leroy said in an article, “Can’t work in L.A. unless you’re a man, a friend” – or whatever it was, because it was Shelly Manne and His Men, Shorty Rogers and His Giants – yeah, yeah, “a man, a friend, or a giant.” [laughter] It probably had some…
When did you first know that this is what you wanted to do?
